acceptance.given: An external Toolchain process has been started through the replay execution path with its configured time and output bounds.

oracle.expected: The execution result records one deterministic terminal category; budget exhaustion is unsuccessful and does not leave an indeterminate terminal state.
oracle.observable: The replay execution result produced by the bounded process records its terminal category and bounded-execution outcome.

acceptance.then: The process reaches a deterministically identified terminal state.
acceptance.when: When the bounded external-process test is evaluated after the process terminates.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Execute the authored S30 bounded-process test with a fixture that produces an otherwise unclassifiable terminal outcome, and observe the behavior test fail until deterministic terminal categorization is implemented.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Make the Toolchain bounded process executor and replay entrypoint classify every external-process completion deterministically, with budget exhaustion unsuccessful.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve existing terminal categories and fail closed for any unrecognized completion; no persistence or schema migration is authorized.

slice_hint.state_transition: executing external process -> deterministically categorized terminal result
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The authored S30 selector observes a deterministic terminal category for each completion and rejects budget exhaustion as unsuccessful.

acceptance.given: A Matrix Case has immutable Stable and Candidate subjects available for two-sided execution.

oracle.expected: The case evidence distinguishes Stable and Candidate fixture identities and execution state for both subject runs.
forbidden: Stable and Candidate subjects sharing a fixture.
Stable and Candidate subjects sharing execution state.
oracle.observable: The authored matrix test inspects the fixture and state identities bound to the Stable and Candidate executions.

acceptance.then: Stable and Candidate executions use distinct fixtures and state.
acceptance.when: When the authored S7 Matrix Case selector evaluates a two-sided Stable/Candidate execution.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Execute the authored S7 matrix test with Stable and Candidate bound to a shared fixture or execution-state identity, and observe the constraint check fail.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Require each Matrix Case to bind Stable and Candidate executions to distinct immutable fixtures and execution state, and preserve attributable evidence for each subject.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve existing replay interfaces; reject shared fixture or execution-state bindings instead of reusing evidence across subjects.

slice_hint.state_transition: unseparated Stable/Candidate execution inputs -> distinct fixture and state bindings per Matrix Case
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The authored S7 selector rejects a Matrix Case whenever Stable and Candidate share fixture or execution state, and accepts only distinct subject bindings.

acceptance.given: A Toolchain plan or replay operation proposes a write whose target resolves under a Hosted workspace path.

oracle.expected: The boundary evaluator rejects the write and the Hosted workspace target remains outside the Toolchain write set.
forbidden: Allowing a Hosted workspace boundary write during TC-D1 work.
oracle.observable: The authored S36 boundary test evaluates a Hosted-workspace write target against the Toolchain write-boundary policy.

acceptance.then: The write is rejected and the Hosted workspace path remains unchanged.
acceptance.when: When the authored S36 selector evaluates a proposed Toolchain write before any write is performed.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Execute the authored S36 boundary test with a Hosted workspace write target and observe the structural write-boundary check fail if the target is admitted.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Reject proposed Toolchain writes that resolve to Hosted workspace paths before execution, without modifying any Phase or runtime implementation.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No Hosted workspace state or Phase service schema may be changed; restore only Toolchain replay write-target validation behavior.

slice_hint.state_transition: proposed Hosted workspace write -> rejected before execution with no workspace mutation
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The authored S36 selector proves that a resolved Hosted workspace write target is rejected before write execution and no forbidden implementation path is in the Toolchain write set.

acceptance.given: A matrix aggregate has evidence whose bound freshness identity is stale.

oracle.expected: The aggregate is marked invalid and cannot be accepted.
forbidden: The aggregate remaining valid despite stale matrix evidence.
Acceptance of the aggregate despite stale matrix evidence.
oracle.observable: The authored S24 test evaluates the aggregate freshness check and its acceptance eligibility from stale matrix evidence.

acceptance.then: The aggregate is invalid because the matrix evidence is stale.
acceptance.when: When the authored S24 selector evaluates aggregate evidence after a bound matrix input becomes stale.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Execute the authored S24 aggregation test with stale matrix evidence and observe the governance constraint check fail if the aggregate remains valid or acceptance-eligible.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Invalidate and make acceptance-ineligible any aggregate whose bound matrix evidence is stale.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve existing replay result compatibility; stale evidence remains a failure condition and cannot be normalized into a valid aggregate.

slice_hint.state_transition: aggregate evaluated with stale matrix evidence -> aggregate invalid and acceptance-ineligible
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The authored S24 selector proves that stale bound matrix evidence yields an invalid aggregate that cannot be accepted.
